problem: Planners on top of pretrained latent world models still use hand-designed update rules (CEM, MPPI, gradient descent) needing thousands of world-model rollouts per decision. Learned planners either imitate a conventional optimizer, use planning to train an amortized policy, or optimize only the next action. Latent Euclidean distance also need not reflect temporal reachability.
motivation: Humans plan by mentally simulating outcomes with an internal model, but ML planning rules are fixed and must be re-tuned per task and model. A planner that learns how to improve whole multi-step plans could be far cheaper and more adaptive. Latent-distance objectives can mis-rank goals (Theorem 1), so a learned cost-to-go critic is also needed.
key_idea: Learn the plan-update rule itself: a neural operator maps (current plan, terminal critic value, value gradient through the frozen world model) to an improved plan and is trained by backpropagating the terminal cost-to-go through unrolled imagined refinement.
insight: With the same learned critic, hand-designed planners largely saturate TwoRoom, so the critic fixes the objective failure while RP1 matches them with about 1000x fewer rollouts (9 vs 9000). The learned update helps most when precision matters (Reacher tau=0.05: 95.3 vs best baseline 80.3 on LeWM; Cube hard scores far above CEM). The critic (latent L2 vs value) comparison and the Dyna result show that residual error is often world-model hallucination, not search quality.
method: Critic: goal-conditioned quasimetric cost-to-go V(z,z_g) (metric residual network) trained offline via hindsight relabeling, n-step TD and expectile regression (tau<0.5) on cached frozen-encoder latents.

Learned planner F_theta: takes plan a_k, terminal value v_k and gradient g_k=grad_a V(H(a_k,z_t),z_g); outputs a_{k+1}. It gets no raw state or goal latents, so it must learn an update rule rather than a policy.

RP1 residual refiner: a_{k+1}=clip(a_k+f_theta(...)), starting from a_0=0, a 3-layer MLP (width 512, ~0.46M params on Cube), weight-tied over K=8 refinement steps; open-loop plans of 5 chunks x 5 primitive actions.

Training: unrolls K refinement steps through the frozen world model, minimizing the final terminal value plus lambda_mean times the mean intermediate values (lambda=0.3); fully offline, environment episodes used only for checkpoint selection.
Dyna finetuning: deploy planner, collect failure rollouts, finetune the world model with a latent anchor, retrain the planner to reduce world-model hallucination exploitation.

Theory: Thm 1 (prediction doesn't identify Euclidean latent geometry, any invertible linear reparameterization stays exact); Thm 2 (a universal learned update rule strictly beats any single fixed optimizer configuration under task heterogeneity, expressivity only).

setting.backbone: RP1 refiner MLP + quasimetric critic, on frozen LeWorldModel and PLDM world models
setting.training_data: Offline trajectories: 10,000 episodes per domain (episodes 0-7999 for training); Dyna adds 1,800 on-policy episodes at each of h25/h100 per round
setting.observation: pixel images encoded into latents by a frozen world-model encoder (Reacher uses a two-frame latent window)
setting.action_space: continuous actions, 5 chunks of 5 primitive actions (25-step horizon), open-loop, replan every 5 chunks
setting.privileged: none at test time (checkpoint selection uses simulator evaluation on held-out selection draws)

numbers.extra: 9 world-model rollouts per decision; median over 6 seeds, 3 draws x 50 episodes
9 rollouts; h25 and h100; easy = raw, hard = normalized to no-op floor
one Dyna round, chosen on validation

numbers_note: No standard navigation benchmarks; TwoRoom is a custom visual-navigation task. Splits are held-out episodes 8000-9999 with draws 42-44, so 'test' is a label choice. Latency (LeWM, Cube h25): RP1 30 ms (B=1), 79 ms (B=50) vs CEM 390.6/5308.2 ms.
results: RP1 with 9 world-model rollouts matches or beats CEM (9000 rollouts), MPPI, Adam, DMPO and L2O-MPC across TwoRoom, Reacher and Cube on LeWM and PLDM. On Cube LeWM h25 hard, RP1 gets 83.4 vs 54.5 for CEM with value critic, and Dyna raises it to 88.6. It plans 13x faster than CEM for one planner and 67x with 50 concurrent planners.
limitations: Trained through a frozen world model, so it exploits model errors and hallucinations; Dyna reduces but does not eliminate this.
Must be retrained per world model and goal horizon; baselines were run at prior-work budgets, not swept, and no amortized-policy comparison.
Checkpoint selection uses simulator evaluation, and only open-loop planning was tested in simple simulated domains.
